chunks: From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad together, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Aban, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when Noah (peace be upon him) planted the seed, his people passed by him and began to laugh and mock, saying, 'He has become a planter.' Until when the palm trees grew tall and became mighty and long, he cut them and then carved them, so they said, 'He has become a carpenter.' Then he assembled them and made them a ship. So they passed by him, laughing and mocking, saying, 'He has become a navigator in the wilderness of the earth,' until he finished it.
ai.seo_question: How did Noah's people react to his shipbuilding process?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the psychological resilience of Prophet Noah (as) by detailing three distinct phases of mockery—planting, carpentry, and navigation—emphasizing that divine mission often requires enduring ridicule during the preparatory stages. In Shia exegesis, this narrative underscores the concept of *istiqamah* (steadfastness) and serves as a paradigm for believers who must remain patient with the skepticism of their contemporaries while executing God's command. The progression from a simple seed to a massive vessel symbolizes the gradual unfolding of divine will amidst human doubt.

en.hubeali: H 14873 – From him, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad together, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali, from Umar Bin Abaan, from Ismail Al-Ju’fy, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’farasws has said that:

‘When Noah<sup>as</sup> planted the seeds, his<sup>as</sup> people passed by him. They laughed at him<sup>as</sup> and were mocking him<sup>as</sup> and were saying, ‘He<sup>as</sup> has become a planter (farmer)’, until the trees became tall and mighty, he<sup>as</sup> cut them, then carved them. So they said, ‘He<sup>as</sup> has become a carpenter’. Then he<sup>as</sup> composed it into a ship. So they passed by him<sup>as</sup> laughing, and mocking, and they were saying, ‘He<sup>as</sup> has become a navigator in the wilderness of the earth’, until he<sup>as</sup> completed it’.
en.sarwar: 426. Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hassan Bin Salih Al-Sawry, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘

The ship of Noah (as) was of the length of a thousand and two hundred cubits, and its width was of eight hundred cubits, and its height in the sky was eighty cubits, and its occupied the space in between Al-Saffa and Al-Marwa, and circled the House seven rounds, then settled upon Al-Joudy’.
